# Yusen Opens 1.1M sq ft Northampton Warehouse Featuring Robotics and Four‑Way Conveyor — First Deployment of System Outside China

Kate Bradbrook - in Northampton; Louise Parry| BBC

Sep 27• 3 min read 4 Save

Brian Luck says the Northampton warehouse is a "pioneering site" with its robotic system [Kate Bradbrook/BBC]

Yusen Logistics UK has opened a 1.1 million sq ft distribution centre near Northampton that uses an advanced robotics and four‑way conveyor system previously seen only in China. The site currently employs about 150 people, with plans to expand to 500–900 as operations grow, and shifts the workforce toward more technical and engineering roles. Around 25% of the warehouse will be temperature‑controlled for pharmaceuticals, and the facility includes sustainability features such as solar panels and rainwater harvesting. Yusen also hopes to connect the site to the delayed Northampton Gateway rail interchange in future.

# Campeys opens major warehouse as food logistics drive gathers pace

By Carol Millett 2026-09-29T14:21:00+01:00

Campeys of Selby has opened a new 190,000 sq ft warehouse at Sherburn 42, more than tripling its existing storage capacity, as it continues to expand into the food and retail logistics sector.

The award-winning family firm said the major investment was made after the company won two “significant” new storage contracts with leading food manufacturers.

Combined, the new contracts and current operations will occupy around 50% of the new facility, with the remaining capacity providing substantial scope for future customer growth. 

Campeys said the new site, which is net zero upon opening, represents a major milestone in its development and will strengthen its position as a specialist logistics and storage partner for the food manufacturing and retail sectors.

The site is expected to become fully operational before the end of 2026 and will also become Campeys’ new head office.

# Allegro expands warehouse network

North Somerset fulfilment specialist Allegro is expanding its warehouse capacity across Clevedon and Portishead, marking the next phase of growth and continued investment on e-commerce fulfilment.

The expansion includes the addition of a further warehouse at Allegro’s established Clevedon operation, alongside the recent addition of a new warehouse in Portishead. Together, the new sites will give the business greater capacity to support existing customers and welcome larger e-commerce brands from across the UK.

The additional Clevedon facility will become operational from 1st November 2026, while the newly acquired Portishead warehouse will be operational from 5th October 2026. Together, the new sites add 25,000 sq ft of warehouse space.

The investment follows Allegro’s recent brand refresh and further strengthens its presence in North Somerset, while creating the additional capacity needed to support its ambitious growth plans with e-commerce fulfilment a key focus for the business over the coming years.

# Warehouse pioneers robotics system used in China

Image source, Kate Bradbrook/BBC

Image caption, Brian Luck says the Northampton warehouse is a "pioneering site" with its robotic system

By Kate Bradbrook, in Northampton and Louise Parry

27 September 2026

A new giant warehouse in England's logistics "golden triangle" is adopting pioneering technology previously only used in China, a company said.

Yusen Logistics UK said it will use a robotics and four-way conveyor system at its new site on the edge of Northampton, which will also employ hundreds of staff.

"There are some roles that robots can do better than people, but fundamentally robots don't work without people," said David Evans, the company's managing director.

The Japanese firm opened its 1.1m sq ft (102,193 sq m) site with a fusion ceremony that included a traditional counting song, sushi, and fish and chips.

### VB Distribution has opened its new business park in Lancashire, adding 100,000 sq. ft of bonded warehousing to its national network of depots

Marking the latest milestone in the group’s long-term expansion programme, the site cements VB Distribution’s position as the market leader ahead of the sector’s biggest regulatory shift in a decade.

The site expands the group’s HMRC-approved customs bonded warehouse operation, one of the few in the sector, allowing duty-suspended storage at a scale others cannot match. With the Vaping Products Duty taking effect on 1 October 2026, bonded capacity shapes who can hold stock, manage duty cash flow and keep retailers supplied without price shocks.

“Most of the market is still working out how to survive October. We’ve built for it,” said Natalia Gosciniak, CEO, VB Distribution.

Evri Group has opened a new depot in Gloucester following a £1.3 million investment to strengthen its growing UK network, increase operational capacity across the Southwest and create 37 permanent roles.

Located at Indurent Park Gloucester in Quedgeley, the new facility replaces the existing Tewkesbury operation, which had reached capacity, and forms part of Evri Group’s continued investment in its network following the acquisition of DHL eCommerce UK.

The move created 38 permanent roles across warehouse, driving, operational and management functions, supporting local employment while enhancing the company’s ability to meet growing customer demand.
